1.subject: Botany
1.text:
Assertion : Annual rings are used to calculate the age of tree.
Reason : Secondary growth is not found in bamboo.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
1.sol: Each year the tree forms new cells (secondary growth) arranged in concentric circles called annual rings. These rings show amount of wood produced during one growing season. By counting the annual rings, the age of a tree can be determined. This phenomenon is called dendrochronology. Only plants showing secondary growth show annual rings. Bamboo is a monocot and hence secondary growth is absent in bamboo.
1.meta: Assertion : Annual rings are used to calculate the age of tree. Reason : Secondary growth is not found in bamboo.

116.subject: Botany
116.text:
Assertion : Gram-negative bacteria do not retain the stain when washed with alcohol.
Reason : The outer face of the outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria contains lipopolysaccharides, a part of which is integrated into the membrane lipids.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
116.sol: The technique of staining bacteria was given by a Dutch microbiologist Christian Gram (1884) and this technique is known as Gram staining. In the cell wall of gram +ve bacteria both horizontal and vertical peptide linkages are present due to which mesh is dense and stain does not come out. Futher outer layer of cell wall of Gram +ve bacteria is made up of techoic acid. In the cell wall of gram -ve bacteria, either horizontal or vertical peptide linkages are present, due to which mesh is loose and hence stain comes out when washed with alcohol. Further outermost layer of cell wall of Gram -ve bacteria is made up lipopolysaccharides.

For the given reaction, $K=\frac{[\mathrm{HI}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{I}_2\right]}$
As 1 mole of $\mathrm{H}_2$ reacts with 1 mole of $\mathrm{I}_2$, even at equilibrium, $\left[\mathrm{H}_2\right]=\left[\mathrm{I}_2\right]$
Hence, $K=\frac{[\mathrm{HI}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{I}_2\right]^2} \quad$ or $\quad \sqrt{K}=\frac{[\mathrm{HI}]}{\left[\mathrm{I}_2\right]}=\sqrt{47.6}$ i.e., $[\mathrm{HI}]>\left[\mathrm{I}_2\right]$

1913.subject: Zoology
1913.text: An example of gene therapy is
options: production of injectable hepatitis B vaccine
production of vaccines in food crops like potatoes which can be eaten
introduction of gene for adenosine deaminase in persons suffering from Severe Combined Immuno-deficiency (SCID)
production of test tube babies by artificial insemination and implantation of fertilized eggs.
1913.sol:
On September 14, 1990 researchers at the U.S. National Institutes of Health performed the first (approved) gene therapy procedure on four-year old Ashanti DeSilva. Born with a rare genetic disease called severe combined immune deficiency (SCID), she lacked a healthy immune system, and was vulnerable to every passing germ. Children with this illness usually develop overwhelming infections and rarely survive to adulthood.
In this gene therapy procedure, doctors removed white blood cells from the child's body, let the cells grow in the lab, inserted the missing gene into the cells, and then infused the genetically modified blood cells back into the patient's blood stream. Laboratory test have shown that the therapy strengthened her immune system.

3308.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
3308.text:
The formation of oxide ion $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ from oxygen atom requires an exothermic reaction, followed by an endothermic step as shown below. The process of formation of $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ in gas phase is unfavorable $\left(\Delta H^{\ominus}=+\right.$ ve )$, even though it has stable configuration of the nearest noble gas neon. This is because
$\begin{aligned} & $\mathrm{O}$(g)+e^{-} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{O}^{-}$(g) ; \Delta H^{\ominus}=-141 $\mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ \\ & $\mathrm{O}^{-}$(g)+e^{-} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$(g) ; \Delta H^{\ominus}=+760 $\mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$\end{aligned}
options: $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ has larger size than that of neon
oxygen is more electronegative than neon
$\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ has larger size than oxygen atom
electron repulsion in oxide ion is more which over comes the stability achieved by noble gas configuration.
3308.sol:
The process of formation of $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ in the gas phase is unfavorable even through $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ is isoelectronic with neon. It is due to that electronic repulsion outweighs the stability gained by achieving noble gas configuration. The formation of oxide ion, $\mathrm{O}^{2-}(g)$ from oxygen atom require first an exothermic and then endothermic step.

$\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{O}($g)+e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}^{-}(g) ; $\Delta H^{\ominus}=-141 \mathrm{~kJ}\mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\\
& \mathrm{O}^{-}(g)+e^{-} \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}^{2-}(g) ; $\Delta H^{\ominus}=+760 $\mathrm{~kJ}\mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}When an electron is added$ to \mathrm{O}^{-}anion, there is strong electrostatic repulsion between two negative charge due to this, the second electron gain enthalpy of oxygen is positive.

For a particular element, the order of size of anion, cation and neutral species is anion > element  >  cation.
Cation has smallest size due to greater $\left(Z_{\text{eff }}\right)$ effective nuclear charge.
Size is inversely proportional to $Z_{\text{eff }}$, which is directly proportional to positive charge.

Differentiating, we get

i.e. $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(a + b\right)cos\left(x + c\right) + y - \left(a + b\right)sin\left(x + c\right)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = \left(a + b\right)\left[cos\left(x + c\right) - sin\left(x + c\right)\right]$

Differentiating, we get

$\dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - \left(a + b\right)\left[sin\left(x + c\right) + cos\left(x + c\right)\right]$

$\dfrac{{d}^{3}y}{d{x}^{3}} - \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = - \left(a + b\right)\left[cos\left(x + c\right) - sin\left(x + c\right)\right]$

i.e. $\dfrac{{d}^{3}y}{d{x}^{3}} - \dfrac{{d}^{2}y}{d{x}^{2}} = - \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y$

Hence, order of differential equation is $3$

15108.text: An infinitely long wiré carrying 1 A current in the $+z$ direction is placed at $(1 \mathrm{ cm}, 1 \mathrm{ cm})$. Another wire carrying $1 \mathrm{ A}$ in $+x$ direction is placed at $y=1 \mathrm{ cm}$. If the magnetic field due to this configuration at the origin is $\mathbf{B}$. Let $B_0$ be the magnitude of the field if only the wire at $(1 \mathrm{ cm}, 1 \mathrm{ cm})$ was present, then $\frac{\mathbf{B}}{B_0}$ is
15108.sol:
Given arrangement is shown below
Distance of conductor I from origin, is $$ \begin{aligned} & d=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}=\sqrt{1+1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & d=\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~cm}=\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned} $$ Magnetic field due to wire Iat origin is $$ B_1=\frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2 \pi d} $$ or $\quad B_1=B_0=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi d}$ $$ \left[\therefore I_1=I_2=1 \mathrm{~A}\right] $$ Now, in vector form, $\mathbf{B}_1=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi d}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j}\right)$ $$ =\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi \times \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-2}}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j}\right) $$ And field of conductor II is $$ \begin{aligned} \mathbf{B}_2 & =\frac{\mu_0 I_2}{2 \pi y}(-\hat{k}) \\ & =\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi \times 10^{-2}}(-\hat{k}) \quad\left[\therefore y=1 \mathrm{~cm}=1 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}\right] \end{aligned} $$ Hence, magnetic field due to both conductors, $$ \begin{aligned} & \mathbf{B}=\mathbf{B}_1+\mathbf{B}_2 \\ & =\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{i}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \hat{j}\right) \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-2}}+\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi}(-\hat{k}) \times \frac{1}{10^{-2}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathbf{B}=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi \times 10^{-2}}\left\{\frac{\hat{i}}{2}-\frac{\hat{j}}{2}-\hat{k}\right\} \end{aligned} $$ Hence, ratio $\frac{\mathbf{B}}{B_0}$ is $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathbf{B}}{B_0}=\left(\frac{\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi \times 10^{-2}}\left(\frac{\hat{i}}{2}-\frac{\hat{j}}{2}-\hat{k}\right)}{\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi \times \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-2}}}\right)=\left(\frac{\hat{i}}{2}-\frac{\hat{j}}{2}-\hat{k}\right) \sqrt{2} \\ & \frac{\hat{i}}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}-\sqrt{2} \hat{k} \\ & \frac{\mathbf{B}}{B_0}=\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},-\sqrt{2}\right)\end{aligned}$

19631.subject: Chemistry
19631.text: Which of the following is highly basic?
19631.sol:
The basicity of amines is determined by the availability of the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom for protonation.

In aniline, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with the benzene ring, which decreases its availability for protonation, making it weakly basic.

In diphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with two benzene rings, which further decreases its availability compared to aniline, making it even less basic.

In triphenylamine, the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is involved in resonance with three benzene rings, making it extremely weakly basic or essentially non-basic.

In benzylamine (C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), the lone pair on the nitrogen atom is not involved in resonance with the benzene ring because the nitrogen is separated from the ring by a $CH_{2}$ group. The electron-donating inductive effect of the benzyl group increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, making it significantly more basic than the aromatic amines listed.

Answer: Benzylamine$

20774.subject: Chemistry
20774.text:
The number of electrons with azimuthal quantum numbers $l=1$ and $l=2$ for Cr in the ground state electronic configurations are respectively.
[Given: $\operatorname{Cr}(Z=24)$ ]
20774.sol:
The atomic number of Chromium (Cr) is $Z = 24$.

The ground state electronic configuration of Cr is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{6} 3d^{5} 4s^{1}$.

The azimuthal quantum number $l$ corresponds to the subshells as follows: $l=0$ for $s$, $l=1$ for $p$, $l=2$ for $d$, and $l=3$ for $f$.

For $l=1$ (p-orbitals), the electrons are in $2p^{6}$ and $3p^{6}$. The total number of electrons is $6 + 6 = 12$.

For $l=2$ (d-orbitals), the electrons are in $3d^{5}$. The total number of electrons is $5$.

Thus, the number of electrons with $l=1$ is $12$ and with $l=2$ is $5$.

Answer: 12 and 5

21456.subject: Mathematics
21456.text: $\text{ Which of the following function is injective? }$
21456.sol:
A function $f(x)$ is injective if $f(x_1) = f(x_2)$ implies $x_1 = x_2$.

For option (LZ8Jm), the function $f(x) = \dfrac{4x^2 + 3x - 5}{4 + 3x - 5x^2}$ is a rational function. It is not injective as it is not monotonic over its entire domain.

For option (fCqBV), $f(x) = (x-4)(x-5) = x^2 - 9x + 20$. This is a parabola opening upwards, which is not injective on $(-\infty, \infty)$ because $f(4) = f(5) = 0$.

For option (bVs0N), $f(x) = |x+2|$ for $x \in [-2, \infty)$. Since $x \ge -2$, $x+2 \ge 0$, so $f(x) = x+2$. This is a linear function with a positive slope, which is strictly increasing. Therefore, it is injective.

For option (FeHkA), $f(x) = x^2 + 2$ is a parabola symmetric about the $y$-axis, so $f(x) = f(-x)$. Thus, it is not injective.

Answer: $f(x)=|x+2|, x \in[-2, \infty)$

21947.subject: Mathematics
21947.text: A student answers a multiple choice question with 5 alternatives, of which exactly one is correct. The probability that he knows the correct answer is $p, 0 < p < 1$. If he does not know the correct answer, he randomly ticks one answer. Given that he has answered the question correctly, the probability that he did not tick the answer randomly, is
21947.sol:
Let $K$ be the event that the student knows the correct answer, and $R$ be the event that the student ticks the answer randomly. Let $C$ be the event that the student answers the question correctly.

The probability that the student knows the answer is $P(K) = p$. The probability that the student does not know the answer is $P(K^{c}) = 1 - p$.

If the student knows the answer, the probability of answering correctly is $P(C|K) = 1$. If the student does not know the answer, the student ticks randomly among 5 alternatives, so the probability of answering correctly is $P(C|K^{c}) = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Using the law of total probability, the probability of answering correctly is $P(C) = P(C|K)P(K) + P(C|K^{c})P(K^{c}) = 1 \times p + \dfrac{1}{5} \times (1 - p) = p + \dfrac{1 - p}{5} = \dfrac{5p + 1 - p}{5} = \dfrac{4p + 1}{5}$.

We want to find the probability that the student knew the answer given that the answer is correct, which is $P(K|C)$. Using Bayes theorem, $P(K|C) = \dfrac{P(C|K)P(K)}{P(C)} = \dfrac{1 \times p}{\dfrac{4p + 1}{5}} = \dfrac{5p}{4p + 1}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5 p}{4 p+1}$

22118.subject: Mathematics
22118.text: For what value of $\mathrm{a}$ and $\mathrm{b}$ the intercepts cut off on the co-ordinate axes by the line $a x-b y+8=0$ are equal in length but opposite in signs to those cut off by the line $2 x-3 y+6=0$ on the axes
22118.sol:
The equation of the line is $2x - 3y + 6 = 0$.

Rewriting in intercept form $\dfrac{x}{A} + \dfrac{y}{B} = 1$:

$2x - 3y = -6 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{-3} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$.

The intercepts are $A = -3$ and $B = 2$.

The intercepts of the line $ax - by + 8 = 0$ are equal in length but opposite in sign to these, so the intercepts are $A' = -(-3) = 3$ and $B' = -(2) = -2$.

The equation of the line with intercepts $A'$ and $B'$ is $\dfrac{x}{3} + \dfrac{y}{-2} = 1$.

Multiplying by 6 gives $2x - 3y = 6$, or $2x - 3y - 6 = 0$.

Comparing $ax - by + 8 = 0$ with the line having intercepts $3$ and $-2$, we first write the line $ax - by = -8$ as $\dfrac{x}{-8/a} + \dfrac{y}{8/b} = 1$.

Equating the intercepts: $-\dfrac{8}{a} = 3 \Rightarrow a = -\dfrac{8}{3}$ and $\dfrac{8}{b} = -2 \Rightarrow b = -4$.

Answer: $a=-\dfrac{8}{3} \quad b=-4$

23025.subject: Physics
23025.text: To increase the current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by $25 \%$, its resistance is increased so that the new resistance becomes twice its initial resistance. By what factor does the voltage sensitivity change?
23025.sol:
The current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer is given by $I_s = \dfrac{\theta}{I} = \dfrac{NAB}{k}$, where $N$ is the number of turns, $A$ is the area, $B$ is the magnetic field, and $k$ is the torsional constant of the spring.

The voltage sensitivity is given by $V_s = \dfrac{\theta}{V} = \dfrac{\theta}{IR} = \dfrac{I_s}{R}$, where $R$ is the resistance of the galvanometer.

Let the initial current sensitivity be $I_{s1}$ and initial resistance be $R_1$. The initial voltage sensitivity is $V_{s1} = \dfrac{I_{s1}}{R_1}$.

The new current sensitivity is $I_{s2} = I_{s1} + 0.25 I_{s1} = 1.25 I_{s1} = \dfrac{5}{4} I_{s1}$.

The new resistance is $R_2 = 2 R_1$.

The new voltage sensitivity is $V_{s2} = \dfrac{I_{s2}}{R_2} = \dfrac{1.25 I_{s1}}{2 R_1} = 0.625 \dfrac{I_{s1}}{R_1} = 0.625 V_{s1}$.

The change in voltage sensitivity is $V_{s2} - V_{s1} = 0.625 V_{s1} - V_{s1} = -0.375 V_{s1}$.

The percentage change is $-0.375 \times 100 \% = -37.5 \%$.

The negative sign indicates a decrease of $37.5 \%$.

Answer: Decreases by $37.5 \%$

25369.text: If $w=\alpha+i \beta$, where $\beta \neq 0$ and $z \neq 1$ satisfies the condition that $\left(\frac{w-\bar{w} z}{1-z}\right)$ is purely real, then the set of values of $z$ is
25369.sol:
Let $z_1=\frac{w-\bar{w}_z}{1-z}$, be purely real.
$ \begin{array}{rlrl}
\Rightarrow & z_1 & =\bar{z}_1 \\
& \therefore & \frac{w-\bar{w} z}{1-z} & =\frac{\bar{w}-w \bar{z}}{1-\bar{z}} \\
\Rightarrow & & w-w \bar{z}-\bar{w} z+\bar{w} z \cdot \bar{z} & =\bar{w}-z \bar{w}-w \bar{z}+w z \cdot \bar{z} \\
\Rightarrow & & (w-\bar{w})+(\bar{w}-w)|z|^2 & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & & (w-\bar{w})\left(1-|z|^2\right) & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & & |z|^2 & =1 \\
\Rightarrow & & |z| & =1 \text{ and } z \neq 1 .
\end{array}   \text{ [as, }$ w-\bar{w} \neq 0 $\text{, since }$ \beta \neq 0 $\text{ ] } $

25823.text: Let ${a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, \ldots$ be an arithmetic progression with ${a}_{1} = 7$ and common difference $8$. Let ${T}_{1}, {T}_{2}, {T}_{3}, \ldots$ be such that ${T}_{1} = 3$ and ${T}_{n + 1} - {T}_{n} = {a}_{n}$ fo $n \ge 1$. Then, which of the following is/are TRUE?
25823.sol:
Given,

${a}_{n} = 7 + \left(n - 1\right)8$ and ${T}_{1} = 3$

Also ${T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{n} + {a}_{n}$

Now ${T}_{n} = {T}_{n - 1} + {a}_{n - 1}$

Putting $n = 1$ we get,

${T}_{2} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1}$

Now putting $n = 2$ we get,

${T}_{3} = {T}_{2} + {a}_{2} ⇒ {T}_{3} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1} + {a}_{2}$

And so on we get,

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + {a}_{1} + {a}_{2} + \ldots + {a}_{n}$

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + \dfrac{n}{2}\left[2\left(7\right) + \left(n - 1\right)8\right]$

$⇒ {T}_{n + 1} = {T}_{1} + n\left(4n + 3\right) ⋯ \left(1\right)$

Now for $n = 19$ we get,

${T}_{20} = 3 + \left(19\right)\left(79\right) = 1504$

And for $n = 29$ we get,

${T}_{30} = 3 + \left(29\right)\left(119\right) = 3454$ {option C is correct}

Now finding sum we get,

$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{20}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 2}^{20}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{19}\left(3 + 4{n}^{2} + 3n\right)$

$= 3 + 3\left(19\right) + \dfrac{3\left(19\right)\left(20\right)}{2} + \dfrac{4\left(19\right)\left(20\right)\left(39\right)}{6}$

$= 3 + 10507 = 10510$ {option B is correct}

And Similarly $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{30}{T}_{k} = 3 + \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{29}\left(4{n}^{2} + 3n + 3\right) = 35615$

27408.subject: Chemistry
27408.text: Identify the incorrect statement about tertiary structure of proteins.
options: They can be fibrous or globular in structure.
The main forces that stabilize the structure are hydrogen bonding, disulphide links, van der Waals and electrostatic forces of attraction.
The structure remains intact when exposed to pH changes.
A linear polypeptide chain will convert to a secondary structure and then further folding of the secondary structure will convert to tertiary structure.
27408.sol:
The tertiary structure of proteins represents the overall folding of the polypeptide chains, which is the further folding of the secondary structure. This folding gives rise to two major molecular shapes: fibrous and globular.

The main forces that stabilize the secondary and tertiary structures of proteins are hydrogen bonds, disulphide linkages, van der Waals forces, and electrostatic forces of attraction.

When a protein in its native form is subjected to physical changes like temperature or chemical changes like pH, the hydrogen bonds and other stabilizing forces are disturbed. Due to this, globules unfold and the helix gets uncoiled, causing the protein to lose its biological activity. This process is called denaturation of the protein. Thus, the tertiary structure does not remain intact when exposed to pH changes.

Answer: The structure remains intact when exposed to pH changes.

31865.subject: Chemistry
31865.text:
How many grams of residue is obtained by heating $2.76$ g of silver carbonate?
(Given: Molar mass of C, O and Ag are $12$, $16$ and $108$ g mol$^{-1}$ respectively)
31865.sol:
Molar mass of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $2 \times 108 + 12 + 3 \times 16 = 276$ g mol$^{-1}$

Number of moles of $Ag_2CO_3$ = $\dfrac{2.76}{276} = 0.01$ mol

The decomposition reaction of silver carbonate on heating is:

$Ag_2CO_3(s) \rightarrow 2Ag(s) + CO_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2}O_2(g)$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $1$ mole of $Ag_2CO_3$ gives $2$ moles of Ag as residue.

Number of moles of Ag formed = $2 \times 0.01 = 0.02$ mol

Mass of Ag residue = $0.02 \times 108 = 2.16$ g

Answer: $2.16$ g

33138.text: The area of the region $\left\{\left(x, y\right)$: {x}^{2} \le y \le 8 - {x}^{2}, y \le 7\right\}$ is $
33138.sol:
The given curves are ${x}^{2} \le y, y \le 8 - {x}^{2}\text{and}y \le 7$

The point of intersection of the curves ${x}^{2} \le y\text{and}y \le 8 - {x}^{2}$ is obtained by,

$⇒ {x}^{2} = 8 - {x}^{2}$

$⇒ x = \pm 2$ and $y = 4$.

Hence the points are $\left(2, 4\right), \left(- 2, 4\right)$.

The points of intersection of the curves $y \le 8 - {x}^{2}\text{and}y \le 7$ is obtained by,

$⇒ 8 - {x}^{2} = 7$

$⇒ x = \pm 1$ and $y = 7$

Hence the points are $\left(1, 7\right), \left(- 1, 7\right)$.

The required graph is

The required area is symmetrical about $y -$axis.

Hence required area is $A = 2\left[{∫}_{0}^{4}\sqrt{y} d y + {∫}_{4}^{7}\sqrt{8 - y} d y\right]$

$A = 2\left[{\left[\dfrac{{y}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right]}_{0}^{4} - {\left[\dfrac{{\left(8 - y\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2}}}{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right]}_{4}^{7}\right]$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left[\left(4\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \left(0\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \left\{\left(8 - 7\right)\dfrac{3}{2} - \left(8 - 4\right)\dfrac{3}{2}\right\}\right]$

$= \dfrac{4}{3}\left(8 - 0 - 1 + 8\right)$

$= 20$ sq units.

Hence, the required area is $20$ sq units.

39155.text:
A slab of dielectric constant $K$ has the same crosssectional area as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor and thickness $\dfrac{3}{4}d$, where $d$ is the separation of the plates. The capacitance of the capacitor when the slab is inserted between the plates will be :

From the above diagram, we can write,

$x + y + \dfrac{3d}{4} = d$

$x + y = \dfrac{d}{4}$

Initially, when there is no dielectric inserted between the plates the capacitance will be, ${C}_{0} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{d}$.

When the dielectric slab is inserted, we can assume there are $3$ capacitors that are connected in series.

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{x}$, ${C}_{2} = \dfrac{4K{ϵ}_{0}A}{3d}$ and ${C}_{3} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{y}$

The equivalent capacitance,

$\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{C}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{C}_{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{C}_{3}} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{ϵ}_{0}A}\left(x + \dfrac{3d}{4K} + y\right) ⇒ \dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{{ϵ}_{0}A}\left(\dfrac{d}{4} + \dfrac{3d}{4K}\right) ⇒ C = \dfrac{4{ϵ}_{0}AK}{d\left(3 + K\right)} ⇒ C = \dfrac{4K{C}_{0}}{3 + K}$

39611.text: A wire of resistance $160 Ω$ is melted and drawn in a wire of one-fourth of its length. The new resistance of the wire will be
39611.sol:
The formula to calculate the resistance of the original wire is given by

$R = ρ\dfrac{l}{A} . . . \left(1\right)$

When the new wire is formed, its resistance is given by

$R ' = ρ\dfrac{l '}{4A} . . . \left(2\right)$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the new resistance.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{R '}{R} & = & \dfrac{ρ\dfrac{l '}{4A}}{ρ\dfrac{l}{A}} \\ & ⇒ & R ' = R\dfrac{l '}{4l} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

41406.subject: Physics
41406.text:
A circular coil of radius $2$ cm and $125$ turns carries a current of $1$ A. The coil is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.4$ T. The axis of the coil makes an angle of $30°$ with the direction of the magnetic field. The torque acting on the coil is $\alpha \times 10^{-4}$ N.m. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
($\pi=3.14$)
41406.sol:
The magnetic moment of the coil is given by $M = NIA$.

The torque acting on the coil is $\tau = MB \sin\theta = NIAB \sin\theta$.

Substituting the given values:

$\tau = 125 \times 1 \times (\pi \times (0.02)^2) \times 0.4 \times \sin 30^\circ$

$\tau = 125 \times 1 \times 4\pi \times 10^{-4} \times 0.4 \times 0.5$

$\tau = 100\pi \times 10^{-4}$

$\tau = 100 \times 3.14 \times 10^{-4} = 314 \times 10^{-4}$ N.m

Comparing with $\alpha \times 10^{-4}$ N.m, we get $\alpha = 314$.

Answer: $314$

53773.text: In the set $Q^{+}$ of all positive rational numbers, the operation * is defined by the formula $a * b=\frac{a b}{6}$. Then, the inverse of 9 with respect to * is
53773.sol:
Let $e$ be the identity,
$\begin{array}{lrl}
\therefore & a^* e & =a \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{a e}{6} & =a \\
\Rightarrow & e & =6 \\
\because & a^* a^{-1} & =e \\
\therefore & a^* a^{-1} & =6 \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{a a^{-1}}{6}=6 \\
\Rightarrow & a^{-1}=\frac{6 \times 6}{a} \\
\therefore & 9^{-1}=\frac{6 \times 6}{9}=4
\end{array}$

59551.subject: Chemistry
59551.text: According to the kinetic molecular theory of gases, the average kinetic energy of gas molecules:
options: Is directly proportional to the absolute temperature
Is the same for all gases at the same volume
59551.sol:
According to the kinetic molecular theory of gases, the average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is given by $E = \dfrac{3}{2}kT$, where $k$ is the Boltzmann constant and $T$ is the absolute temperature.

For one mole of an ideal gas, the average kinetic energy is $E = \dfrac{3}{2}RT$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant.

This shows that the average kinetic energy of gas molecules depends only on the absolute temperature and is directly proportional to it. It is independent of pressure, volume, and the nature of the gas.

Answer: Is directly proportional to the absolute temperature

61577.text:
In a certain culture of bacteria, the rate of increase is proportional to the number
present. It is found that the number doubles in 4 hours. Then the number of times
the bacteria are increased in 12 hours is
61577.sol:
Let $x$ be the number of bacteria in certain culture at time $t$. Then rate of increase is $\frac{d x}{d t}$ which is proportional to $x$.

\therefore \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}} \propto \mathrm{x} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{Kx} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{Kdt} \Rightarrow \int \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{K} \int \mathrm{dt} \\
\therefore \log \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{Kt}+\mathrm{c} ...(1)\\
\text{ Initially when } \mathrm{t}=0, \operatorname{let} \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{x}_{0} \\
\therefore \log \mathrm{x}=0+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\log \mathrm{x}_{0} \\
\therefore \text{ from }(1) \log \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{kt}+\log \mathrm{x}_{0} \\
\therefore \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{x}_{0}}\right)=\mathrm{Kt}...(2)
\end{array}$
Given number doubles in 4 hrs i.e. when $ t=4, x=2 x_{0}\therefore $\log\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{x}_{0}}{\mathrm{x}_{0}}\right)=4 \mathrm{ K} \Rightarrow \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{4} \log2\therefore$ from (2) $\log\left(\frac{x}{x_{0}}\right)=\frac{t}{4} \log2 
When \mathrm{t}= 12\log \left(\frac{x}{x_{0}}\right)=\frac{12}{4} \log2=3 \log 2=\log 2^{3}=\log 8\therefore \frac{x}{x_{0}}=8 \Rightarrow x=8 x_{0}$
This problem can be alternatively solved as follows :
Let the intial number of bacteria be \mathrm{x}$$.
$\therefore$ Number of bacteria after 4 $\mathrm{hrs}=$2 $\mathrm{x}$

62961.text: If $\mathrm{p} \equiv$ The switch $\mathrm{S}_1$ is closed, $\mathrm{q} \equiv$ The switch $\mathrm{S}_2$ is closed, $\mathrm{r} \equiv$ switch $S_3$ is closed, then symbolic form of following switching circuit is equivalent to
62961.sol:
Representing switch states as propositions: $p$ for "The switch S1 is closed", $q$ for "The switch S2 is closed", and $r$ for "The switch S3 is closed".

In switching algebra, series connections correspond to logical AND and parallel connections to logical OR, while an open switch $S^{\prime}$ corresponds to the negation of the proposition for the closed switch. The circuit has two parallel branches. The upper branch consists of S1 in series with the parallel combination of S2 and S3, represented as $p \wedge (q \vee r)$. The lower branch is a series connection of $S3^{\prime}$, $S2^{\prime}$, and S1, represented as $ eg r \wedge eg q \wedge p$. The complete symbolic equivalent is the OR of these two expressions: $[p \wedge (q \vee r)] \vee [ eg r \wedge eg q \wedge p]$. Rearranging terms and factoring gives $p \wedge [(q \vee r) \vee ( eg q \wedge eg r)]$. Using De Morgan's law: $ eg q \wedge eg r \equiv eg (q \vee r)$. Substituting and introducing $X = q \vee r$ yields $X \vee eg X$, which is a tautology T. The expression simplifies to $p \wedge T$, which is equivalent to $p$.

Final answer: $ oxed{A}$

Number of trials, $n = 4$

Number of successes, $r = 2$

$P(X = 2) = \dfrac{54}{256} = \dfrac{27}{128}$

63618.subject: Mathematics
63618.text: A box contains 8 red and $x$ number of green balls. 3 balls are drawn at random, if the probability that 3 balls being red is $\frac{7}{15}$ then number of green balls is _______
63618.sol:
Let $R = 8$ be the number of red balls and $G = x$ be the number of green balls.
The total number of balls is then $N = R + G = 8 + x$.

The total number of ways to draw 3 balls is $\binom{8 + x}{3} = \frac{(8 + x)(7 + x)(6 + x)}{6}$.
The number of ways to draw exactly 3 red balls is $\binom{8}{3} = 56$.

Given that the probability of drawing 3 red balls is $\frac{7}{15}$, the equation becomes:
$\frac{7}{15} = \frac{56}{\frac{(8 + x)(7 + x)(6 + x)}{6}} = \frac{336}{(8 + x)(7 + x)(6 + x)}$.

Rearranging gives:
$(8 + x)(7 + x)(6 + x) = \frac{336 \times 15}{7} = 720$.

The product of three consecutive integers $(6 + x)$, $(7 + x)$, and $(8 + x)$ must equal 720.
Testing options:

  • $x = 2$: $10 \cdot 9 \cdot 8 = 720$
  • $x = 4$: $12 \cdot 11 \cdot 10 = 1320$
  • $x = 3$: $11 \cdot 10 \cdot 9 = 990$
  • $x = 5$: $13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11 = 1716$

Only $x = 2$ satisfies the condition, so the number of green balls is 2.
Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

64212.text: The equation of the line passing through the point of intersection of the lines $x+2 y+6=0$ and $2 x-y=2$ and making an intercept 5 on the $y$-axis is
64212.sol:
The given lines are $x + 2y + 6 = 0$ and $2x - y = 2$, with answer options suggesting the question seeks the angle between them.

Rewriting in slope-intercept form, the first line becomes $y = -\frac{1}{2}x - 3$, with slope $m_1 = -\frac{1}{2}$.

The second line is $y = 2x - 2$, with slope $m_2 = 2$.

The product of slopes is $m_1 \cdot m_2 = -\frac{1}{2} \times 2 = -1$, indicating perpendicular lines.

The angle between perpendicular lines is $\frac{\pi}{2}$ radians.

Thus, the correct option is D.

64422.text: The distance of the point $A(3,-4,5)$ from the plane $2 x+5 y-6 z=16$ measured along the line $\frac{x}{2}=\frac{y}{1}=\frac{z}{-2}$ is
64422.sol:
The distance from $A(3,-4,5)$ to the plane $2x+5y-6z=16$ measured along the direction $(2,1,-2)$ is determined by finding the intersection point of the line through $A$ parallel to this direction with the plane.

The parametric equations of the line are $x=3+2\lambda$, $y=-4+\lambda$, $z=5-2\lambda$. Substituting into the plane equation yields:

$2(3+2\lambda)+5(-4+\lambda)-6(5-2\lambda)=16$

$21\lambda-44=16$

$\lambda=\frac{60}{21}=\frac{20}{7}$

The intersection point coordinates are:

$x_B=3+2\cdot\frac{20}{7}=\frac{61}{7}$

$y_B=-4+\frac{20}{7}=\frac{-8}{7}$

$z_B=5-2\cdot\frac{20}{7}=\frac{-5}{7}$

The distance $AB$ is calculated as:

$\sqrt{\left(\frac{61}{7}-3\right)^2+\left(\frac{-8}{7}+4\right)^2+\left(\frac{-5}{7}-5\right)^2}$

$\sqrt{\left(\frac{40}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac{20}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac{-40}{7}\right)^2}$

$\sqrt{\frac{1600+400+1600}{49}}=\sqrt{\frac{3600}{49}}=\frac{60}{7}$

The distance measured along the given line is $\frac{60}{7}$ units.

65662.subject: Physics
65662.text: Average power associated with an ideal inductor and ideal capacitor over a complete cycle of a.c. is respectively
65662.sol:
1. Ideal Inductor:
- The voltage and current in an ideal inductor are out of phase by 90 degrees, with the current lagging the voltage by $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.
- The instantaneous power is given by $p(t)=v(t) \times i(t)$.
- Over a complete cycle, the positive and negative power values cancel out, resulting in an average power of zero.
2. Ideal Capacitor:
- In an ideal capacitor, the voltage and current are also out of phase by 90 degrees, but this time, the current leads the voltage by $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.
- Similar to the inductor case, the instantaneous power alternates between positive and negative, resulting in an average power of zero over a complete cycle.

66781.subject: Physics
66781.text: A square loop of area $25 \text{ cm}^2$ has a resistance of $10\Omega$. The loop is placed in uniform magnetic field of magnitude $40$ T. The plane of the loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in pulling the loop out of the magnetic field slowly and uniformly in one second will be
66781.sol:
Given:
Area of the loop, $A = 25 \text{ cm}^2 = 25 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$
Resistance, $R = 10 \ \Omega$
Magnetic field, $B = 40 \text{ T}$
Time taken, $\Delta t = 1 \text{ s}$

The total change in magnetic flux as the loop is pulled out of the magnetic field is:
$\Delta \Phi = B A = 40 \times 25 \times 10^{-4} = 0.1 \text{ Wb}$

Since the loop is pulled out uniformly, the rate of change of flux is constant. The induced emf $E$ is:
$E = \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0.1}{1} = 0.1 \text{ V}$

The electrical power dissipated as heat in the loop due to its resistance is:
$P = \dfrac{E^2}{R} = \dfrac{(0.1)^2}{10} = \dfrac{0.01}{10} = 10^{-3} \text{ W}$

The work done by the external agent in pulling the loop out slowly and uniformly is equal to the total heat energy dissipated:
$W = P \Delta t = 10^{-3} \times 1 = 1.0 \times 10^{-3} \text{ J}$

Answer: $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ J

68793.text: The time period of a simple pendulum inside a stationary lift is ' $T$ '. When the lift starts accelerating upwards with an acceleration $\left(\frac{\mathrm{g}}{3}\right)$, the time period of the pendulum will be
68793.sol:
Time period of a simple pendulum is $\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\left(\frac{l}{\mathrm{a}}\right)}$

In stationary lift, the value of acceleration is $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g}$
$$
\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\left(\frac{l}{\mathrm{~g}}\right)}
$$

When the lift is accelerating in an upward direction, there is a pseudo force acting in a downward direction.
$$
\therefore \quad \mathrm{ma}=\mathrm{mg}+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{3}
$$
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g}+\frac{\mathrm{g}}{3}$
$\therefore \quad a=\frac{4 g}{3}$
$\therefore \quad$ Period for a pendulum in accelerating lift is
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{T}^{\prime} & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{\mathrm{a}}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{3 l}{4 \mathrm{~g}}} \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{T}^{\prime} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\left(2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{\mathrm{~g}}}\right) \\
\therefore \quad \mathrm{T}^{\prime} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \mathrm{~T}
\end{aligned}
$$

69193.text: Four particles each of mass $M$ are placed at the corners of a square of side L. The radius of gyration of the system about an axis perpendicular to the square and passing through its centre is
69193.sol:
The axis of rotation passes perpendicularly through the center of the square with side length $L$. Each particle of mass $M$ lies at distance $r = L/\sqrt{2}$ from the center, equal to half the diagonal length.

The moment of inertia for one particle is $Mr^2 = M(L/\sqrt{2})^2 = ML^2/2$. For four identical particles, the total moment of inertia becomes $I_{\text{total}} = 4 \times (ML^2/2) = 2ML^2$.

Using the relationship $I_{\text{total}} = (4M)K^2$ for the system’s total mass $4M$ and radius of gyration $K$, we substitute $2ML^2 = 4MK^2$.

Solving yields $K^2 = L^2/2$, so $K = L/\sqrt{2}$.

The radius of gyration is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

70517.subject: Physics
70517.text: Two pipes of lengths $\mathrm{L}_1$ and $\mathrm{L}_2$, open at both ends are joined in series. If ' $f_1$ ' and ' $f_2$ ' are the fundamental frequencies of two pipes, then the fundamental frequency of series combination will be (neglect end correction)
70517.sol:
Fundamental frequency for an open pipe is given by $f = \frac{v}{2L}$, where $v$ is the speed of sound and $L$ is the pipe length.

The individual pipe lengths are $L_1 = \frac{v}{2f_1}$ and $L_2 = \frac{v}{2f_2}$.

When joined in series, the total length becomes $L_{\text{total}} = L_1 + L_2 = \frac{v}{2}\left(\frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}\right) = \frac{v}{2} \cdot \frac{f_1 + f_2}{f_1 f_2}$.

The fundamental frequency of the combined pipe is then:

$f_{\text{total}} = \frac{v}{2L_{\text{total}}} = \frac{v}{2 \cdot \frac{v}{2} \cdot \frac{f_1 + f_2}{f_1 f_2}} = \frac{1}{\frac{f_1 + f_2}{f_1 f_2}} = \frac{f_1 f_2}{f_1 + f_2}$.

The result corresponds to option C.

70692.text: A cylindrical tube open at both ends has fundamental frequency ' $n$ ' in air. The tube is dipped vertically in water so that one-fourth of it is in water. The fundamental frequency of the air column becomes
70692.sol:
The fundamental frequency of open tube is
$\mathrm{n}_1=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{2 \ell_1}$
When tube is dipped in water, one-fourth of it is in water and three-fourth is in air. Hence, it becomes a tube closed at one end with length $\ell_2=\frac{3}{4} \ell_1$ The fundamental frequency of closed tube is
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{n}_2=\frac{\mathrm{v}}{4 \ell_2} \\
& \therefore \frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1}=\frac{1}{4 \ell_2} \times 2 \ell_1=\frac{\ell_1}{2 \ell_2}=\frac{4}{2 \times 3} \quad\left[\because \frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}=\frac{4}{3}\right] \\
& \therefore \mathrm{n}_2=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{n}_1=\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{n}
\end{aligned}$

71632.sol:
The haloform reaction is given by compounds containing a methyl ketone group ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-}$) or compounds that can be oxidized to this group, such as alcohols containing the $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-}$ group.

Among the given options, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CO}$ (acetone) contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-}$ group and therefore gives a positive haloform test.

$\text{HCHO}$ (formaldehyde) lacks the $\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-}$ group.

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{-O-CH}_3$ do not possess the required structural features to undergo the haloform reaction.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CO}$

71962.subject: Chemistry
71962.text: The silicon doped with gallium forms
71962.sol:
Silicon is a Group 14 element with four valence electrons.

Gallium is a Group 13 element with three valence electrons.

When silicon is doped with gallium, the gallium atoms replace some of the silicon atoms in the crystal lattice.

Since gallium has only three valence electrons, it can form only three covalent bonds with the surrounding silicon atoms.

This creates a vacancy or a hole in the fourth bond, which acts as a positive charge carrier.

Therefore, doping silicon with gallium results in the formation of a p-type semiconductor.

Answer: p-type semiconductor

72270.subject: Physics
72270.text:
There are four lightweight rod samples P, Q, R and S separately suspended by thread. A bar magnet is slowly brought near to each sample and the following observations are noted
(a) P is weakly repelled
(b) R is strongly attracted
(c) S remains unaffected
(d) Q is weakly attracted
Which of the following is true?
options: R is of a diamagnetic material
P is of a non-magnetic material
S is of a ferromagnetic material
Q is of a paramagnetic material
72270.sol:
When a bar magnet is brought near a material, the magnetic behavior can be identified by the interaction:

Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnetic field. Since P is weakly repelled, P is a diamagnetic material.

Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted by a magnetic field. Since R is strongly attracted, R is a ferromagnetic material.

Non-magnetic materials are unaffected by a magnetic field. Since S remains unaffected, S is a non-magnetic material.

Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted by a magnetic field. Since Q is weakly attracted, Q is a paramagnetic material.

Comparing these conclusions with the given options, the statement that Q is of a paramagnetic material is true.

Answer: Q is of a paramagnetic material

79723.subject: Botany
79723.sol:
Vacuoles: Membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm is called vacuole. A vacuole contains water, sap, excretory product and other useless materials. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane; called tonoplast.
The vacuole can occupy up to 90% of the volume in a plant cell. In plant cells, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradient into the vacuole. Hence, their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
In Amoeba, the vacuoles can be contractile vacuoles or food vacuoles. Contractile vacuoles helps in storing up of excretory waste, while food vacuoles helps in storing and gathering foods.

79964.subject: Botany
79964.text: Which of the following is a primary consumer in maize field ecosytem?
79964.sol:
Primary consumers are herbivorous organism, that feed on producers. In a food chain, grasshoppers are primary consumers, phytoplankton are producers, and wolf and lions are secondary and tertiary consumers respectively.
Related Theory
The amount of energy flow decrease with successive trophic levels as only $10 \%$ of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next successive level. The energy is lost in the form of respiration and other vital activities to maintain life. If more trophic levels are present, the residual energy will be limited and decreased to such an extent that it cannot further support any trophic level by the flow of energy. So the food chain is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels only.

84273.subject: Zoology
84273.text: Which of the following hormones is not a secretion product of human placenta?
84273.sol:
Prolactin is secreted by anterior pituitary gland and cause production of milk in mammary glands. Placenta produce estrogen, progesterone, relaxin Human chorionic gonadotropin hormone (hCG) and Human placental lactogen (hPL).
Related Theory
Progesterone acts to maintain pregnancy by supporting the lining of the uterus (womb), which provides the environment for the foetus and the placenta to grow. estrogen is also produced by the placenta during pregnancy to help maintain a healthy pregnancy.
Caution
Circulating relaxin is secreted by the corpus luteum. The placenta, decidua, or both also produce relaxin, which does not enter the circulation but may act in an autocrine or paracrine fashion. hCG is a stimulus to luteal relaxin secretion.

85379.text: Select the option including all sexually transmitted diseases.
85379.sol:
SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES (STDs):
The diseases which are primarily transmitted through sexual intercourse are called sexually transmitted diseases (STD) or venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI). STDs are found across all age groups but are more prevalent in organisms of age 15-24 years.

85384.subject: Zoology
85384.text: Which of the following contraceptive methods do involve a role of hormone?
85384.sol:
(i) Lactational amenorrhea: Breastfeeding delays the resumption of normal ovarian cycles by disrupting the pattern of pulsatile release of GnRH from the hypothalamus due to production of prolactin and hence FSH and LH from the pituitary.
(ii) Progestin-only emergency contraceptive pills (morning after pills) are pills that contain levonorgestrel, a type of the hormone progestin researchers have found prevents pregnancy when taken in the few days after sex.
(iii) There are two main kinds of birth control pills — combination birth control pills, which contain estrogen and progestin.

85799.subject: Biology
85799.text:
Events occurring during signal propagation in a chemical synapse are given below.
P: Postsynaptic membrane potential changes.
Q: Synaptic vesicle fuses with the presynaptic membrane.
R: Action potential depolarizes the presynaptic terminal.
S: Neurotransmitter binds to receptors on the postsynaptic membrane.
T: Neurotransmitter is released into the synaptic cleft.
The correct sequence of occurrence of these events is:
85799.sol:
The sequence of events during signal propagation in a chemical synapse is as follows:

First, an action potential arrives at the axon terminal and depolarizes the presynaptic terminal (R).

This depolarization triggers the influx of calcium ions, causing synaptic vesicles to fuse with the presynaptic membrane (Q).

Following fusion, the neurotransmitter is released into the synaptic cleft via exocytosis (T).

The released neurotransmitter diffuses across the cleft and binds to specific receptors on the postsynaptic membrane (S).

This binding opens ion channels, leading to a change in the postsynaptic membrane potential (P).

Thus, the correct sequence is R, Q, T, S, P.

Answer: R, Q, T, S, P

So, the ratio number of neutrons to that of protons

102026.text:
Answer the following by appropriately matching the lists based on the information given in the paragraph.
In a thermodynamics process on an ideal monatomic gas, the infinitesimal heat absorbed by the gas is given by $T\DeltaX,$ where $T$ is temperature of the system and $\DeltaX$ is the infinitesimal change in a thermodynamic quantity $X$ of the system. For a mole of monatomic ideal gas $X = \dfrac{3}{2}Rln\left(\dfrac{T}{{T}_{A}}\right) + Rln\left(\dfrac{V}{{V}_{A}}\right) .$ Here, $R$ is gas constant, $V$ is volume of gas, ${T}_{A}$ and ${V}_{A}$ are constants.
The List-I below gives some quantities involved in a process and List-II gives some possible values of these quantities.
 

 Column - I Column - II
(a)Work done by the system in process $1 \to 2 \to 3$(p)$\dfrac{1}{3}R{T}_{0}ln2$
(b)Change in internal energy in process $1 \to 2 \to 3$(q)$\dfrac{1}{3}R{T}_{0}$
(c)Heat absorbed by the system in process $1 \to 2 \to 3$(r)$R{T}_{0}$
(d)Heat absorbed by the system in process $1 \to 2$(s)$\dfrac{4}{3}R{T}_{0}$
  (t)$\dfrac{1}{3}R{T}_{0}\left(3 + ln2\right)$
  (u)$\dfrac{5}{6}R{T}_{0}$

If the process on one mole of monatomic ideal gas is as shown in the $PV$ -diagram with ${P}_{0}{V}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{3}R{T}_{0},$ the correct match is
options: $a - s, b - r, c - q, d - t$
$a - q, b - r, c - p, d - u$
$a - q, b - s, c - r, d - u$
$a - q, b - r, c - s, d - u$

$\left(a\right){W}_{1 \to 2 \to 3} = {W}_{1 \to 2} + {W}_{2 \to 3}$
$= {P}_{0}\left[2{V}_{0} - {V}_{0}\right] + 0 = {P}_{0}{V}_{0}$
${W}_{1 \to 2 \to 3} = {P}_{0}{V}_{0}$
$\begin{cases}= \dfrac{R{T}_{0}}{3} & \left(a \to q\right)\end{cases}$
$\left[\begin{array}{ll}\text{Process}1 \to 2 ⇒ \text{isobaric} \\ \text{and}2 \to 3 ⇒ \text{isochoric}\end{array}\right]$


$\left(b\right){U}_{1 \to 2 \to 3} = \dfrac{3}{2}\left[\dfrac{3{P}_{0}}{2} \times 2{V}_{0} - {P}_{0}{V}_{0}\right]$
$\begin{cases}= \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2{P}_{0}{V}_{0} = 3{P}_{0}{V}_{0} = R{T}_{0} & \left(b \to r\right)\end{cases}$


$\left(c\right){Q}_{1 \to 2 \to 3} = {U}_{1 \to 2 \to 3} + {W}_{1 \to 2 \to 3}$
$\begin{cases}= R{T}_{0} + \dfrac{R{T}_{0}}{3} = \dfrac{4R{T}_{0}}{3} & \left(c \to s\right)\end{cases}$


$\left(d\right){Q}_{1 \to 2} = n{C}_{P} ∆ T$

$= \dfrac{5}{2}\left[{P}_{0}2{V}_{0} - {P}_{0}{V}_{0}\right]$

102658.subject: Physics
102658.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the standing waves in organ pipes of length $L$.

List-IList-II (Wavelength $\lambda$)
(A) $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone of a closed pipe(I) $\dfrac{4L}{5}$
(B) $2^{\text{nd}}$ overtone of an open pipe(II) $L$
(C) $2^{\text{nd}}$ overtone of a closed pipe(III) $\dfrac{4L}{3}$
(D) $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone of an open pipe(IV) $\dfrac{2L}{3}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102658.sol:
For a closed organ pipe of length $L$, the allowed frequencies are odd harmonics: $f = (2n+1)\dfrac{v}{4L}$, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$ is the overtone number.
The wavelength is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{4L}{2n+1}$.
(A) $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone of a closed pipe ($n=1$): $\lambda = \dfrac{4L}{3}$. So, (A) matches with (III).
(C) $2^{\text{nd}}$ overtone of a closed pipe ($n=2$): $\lambda = \dfrac{4L}{5}$. So, (C) matches with (I).

For an open organ pipe of length $L$, all harmonics are present: $f = (n+1)\dfrac{v}{2L}$, where $n = 0, 1, 2, \dots$ is the overtone number.
The wavelength is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{2L}{n+1}$.
(B) $2^{\text{nd}}$ overtone of an open pipe ($n=2$): $\lambda = \dfrac{2L}{3}$. So, (B) matches with (IV).
(D) $1^{\text{st}}$ overtone of an open pipe ($n=1$): $\lambda = \dfrac{2L}{2} = L$. So, (D) matches with (II).

The correct matching sequence is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

102888.subject: Physics
102888.text: Two isolated solid conducting spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$ are charged such that they have the same electrostatic potential. What is the ratio of the magnitudes of the electric fields at their respective surfaces ($E_1 : E_2$)?
102888.sol:
The electrostatic potential $V$ at the surface of a conducting sphere of radius $r$ and charge $Q$ is given by $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r}$.

Since both spheres are at the same potential, $V_1 = V_2$.

The electric field $E$ at the surface of a conducting sphere is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{r^2}$.

This can be rewritten in terms of potential as $E = \dfrac{V}{r}$.

Since $V$ is constant for both spheres, the electric field is inversely proportional to the radius ($E \propto \dfrac{1}{r}$).

Therefore, the ratio of their electric fields is:
$\dfrac{E_1}{E_2} = \dfrac{r_2}{r_1} = \dfrac{2R}{R} = \dfrac{2}{1}$

The ratio is $2 : 1$.

Answer: $2 : 1$

107586.text: Match each of the diatomic molecules in Column I with its property/properties in Column II.

- A. \(B_2\) : Has two unpaired electrons, making it p. Paramagnetic. The close energy levels of \(2 s\) and \(2 p\) orbitals lead to \($\mathrm{t.s - p}$\) mixing.
- B. \(\boldsymbol{N}_{\mathrm{2}$}$\) : Has a bond order of \($\mathrm{3}$\), so its bond order is \($\mathrm{s}$\). \($\mathrm{\geq 2}$\). It also has \($\mathrm{t . s - p}$\) mixing and can gain electrons, so it r. Undergoes reduction.

108676.subject: Chemistry
108676.text:
For the reaction $2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$, the heat of reaction at constant volume is $-221.0 \text{ kJ}$ at $300 \text{ K}$. The heat of reaction at constant pressure at the same temperature is:
(Given $R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
108676.sol:
From the First Law of Thermodynamics, heat absorbed at constant volume ($q_v$) is equal to the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$), and heat absorbed at constant pressure ($q_p$) is equal to the change in enthalpy ($\Delta H$).

Given:
$q_v = \Delta U = -221.0 \text{ kJ}$
$T = 300 \text{ K}$
$R = \dfrac{25}{3} \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$

For the reaction $2\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{s}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})$:
$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$
$\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1$ (Solid carbon is not counted).

The relationship between $q_p$ and $q_v$ is:
$q_p = q_v + \Delta n_g RT$

First, calculate the $\Delta n_g RT$ term in kJ:
$\Delta n_g RT = 1 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{3}\right) \times 300 \text{ J}$
$= 2500 \text{ J} = 2.5 \text{ kJ}$

Now, substitute the values:
$q_p = -221.0 \text{ kJ} + 2.5 \text{ kJ}$
$q_p = -218.5 \text{ kJ}$

Note: A common mistake is to include the solid reactant in the $\Delta n_g$ calculation (giving $\Delta n_g = -1$ and an incorrect answer of $-223.5 \text{ kJ}$) or failing to convert the $RT$ term to kJ (giving $+2279 \text{ kJ}$).

Answer: $-218.5 \text{ kJ}$

108714.text: A diatomic gas at pressure $P$, compressed adiabatically to half of its volume, what is the final pressure?

$P_2=P_1\left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^\gamma \quad$ [For diatomic gas, $\gamma=1.4$ ]
$P_2=P_1\left(\frac{V_1 \times 2}{V_1}\right)^{1.4}$
$P_2=P_1(2)^{1.4}=(2)^{1.4} P$

111946.subject: Chemistry
111946.text: The correct decreasing order of the basic strength of ethyl substituted amines and ammonia in aqueous solution is:
111946.sol:
In aqueous solution, the basic strength of amines depends on the combined effect of the inductive effect (+I), solvation (hydrogen bonding with water), and steric hindrance.

For ethyl substituted amines, the larger size of the ethyl group compared to the methyl group causes steric hindrance to play a more significant role, altering the balance between solvation and the +I effect.

The resulting order of basicity for ethylamines in aqueous solution is secondary > tertiary > primary > ammonia. Therefore, the correct decreasing order is $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} > (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 > \text{NH}_3$.

Answer: $(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_2\text{NH} > (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{N} > \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 > \text{NH}_3$

112651.subject: Chemistry
112651.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:
$\text{2-Methylprop-1-ene} \xrightarrow[\text{Peroxide}]{\text{HBr}} \text{X} \xrightarrow[\text{Dry ether}]{\text{Na}} \text{Y}$
The IUPAC name of the major product Y is:
112651.sol:
Step 1: 2-Methylprop-1-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$) reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide to undergo anti-Markovnikov addition. The bromine atom adds to the less substituted carbon, yielding 1-bromo-2-methylpropane as intermediate X.

Step 2: 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane (X) undergoes the Wurtz reaction when treated with sodium in dry ether. Two molecules of the alkyl halide couple together to form an alkane.

$2 \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{NaBr}$

The longest carbon chain has 6 carbon atoms with methyl groups at the 2nd and 5th positions. Thus, the IUPAC name of product Y is 2,5-dimethylhexane.

If Markovnikov addition had occurred (due to the absence of peroxide), the intermediate would be 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, which would lead to 2,2,3,3-tetramethylbutane.

Answer: 2,5-Dimethylhexane

116328.subject: Chemistry
116328.text: Three Xenon compounds A, B, and C have square planar, linear, and square pyramidal geometries respectively. The number of lone pairs on the central Xenon atom in compounds A, B, and C are respectively:
116328.sol:
For a Xenon compound to have a square planar geometry (e.g., $\text{XeF}_4$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization with 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs.

For a linear geometry (e.g., $\text{XeF}_2$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d$ hybridization with 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs.

For a square pyramidal geometry (e.g., $\text{XeOF}_4$), the central Xe atom undergoes $sp^3d^2$ hybridization with 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair.

Therefore, the number of lone pairs on the central Xenon atom in compounds A, B, and C are 2, 3, and 1 respectively.

Answer: 2, 3, 1

121377.subject: Botany
121377.text: What are the types of genetic material found in viruses?
121377.sol: In addition to proteins, <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> viruses also contain genetic material, that could be either RNA or DNA. </mark>  No virus contains both RNA and DNA. A virus is a nucleoprotein and the genetic material is infectious. In general, viruses that infect plants have single stranded RNA and viruses that infect animals have either single or double stranded RNA or double stranded DNA.Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages (viruses that infect the bacteria) are usually double stranded DNA viruses. The protein coat called capsid made of small subunits called capsomeres, protects the nucleic acid. These capsomeres are arranged in helical or polyhedralgeometric forms. Viruses cause diseases like mumps, small pox, herpes and influenza. AIDS in humans is also caused by a virus. In plants, the symptoms can be mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.

121701.subject: Botany
121701.text: Which of the following algae exhibits oogamous reproduction?
121701.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. <mark>Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus</mark>

121746.subject: Botany
121746.text: Which of the following is not mentioned as a common form of brown algae?
121746.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus. Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium (oogamous species). The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella. <mark>The common forms are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.</mark>

121773.subject: Botany
121773.text: What is produced when an antherozoid fuses with an egg in bryophytes?
121773.sol: Bryophytes include the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. They usually occur in damp, humid and shaded localities. They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks/soil. The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. They lack true roots, stems or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte. The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ is called antheridium.They produce biflagellate antherozoids. The female sex organ called archegonium is flask-shaped and produces a single egg. The antherozoids are released into water where they come in contact with archegonium. <mark>An antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote</mark>. Zygotes do not undergo reduction division immediately. They produce a multicellular body called a sporophyte. The sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division (meiosis) to produce haploid spores. These spores germinate to produce gametophyte.

121869.sol: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid, e.g., Marchantia. The thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures. Asexual reproduction in liverworts takes place by fragmentation of thalli, or by the formation of specialised structures called gemmae (sing. gemma). Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds, which develop in small receptacles called gemma cups located on the thalli.

123545.subject: Botany
123545.text: What happens during the cell division process?
123545.sol: All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle. Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle. The replicated chromosomes (DNA) are then distributed to daughter nuclei by a complex series of events during cell division. These events are themselves under genetic control

124277.sol:
Structure Y is the primary site of protein synthesis, which identifies it as the ribosome. Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.

Structure X synthesizes the rRNA component of ribosomes and is a non-membrane bound body located in the nucleoplasm. This identifies structure X as the nucleolus, which is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle. The rough endoplasmic reticulum is a membrane-bound network studded with ribosomes but is not structure Y itself. The centrosome is non-membrane bound but is involved in cell division, not rRNA synthesis.

Answer: X - Nucleolus, Y - Ribosome

124731.text: A vegetable vendor wants to keep harvested leafy vegetables fresh and green for a longer duration before selling them in the market. Which of the following plant growth regulators should be applied to achieve this by delaying leaf senescence?
124731.sol:
Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps in the delay of leaf senescence. Therefore, applying cytokinins helps in keeping leafy vegetables fresh and green for a longer duration.

Ethylene and abscisic acid are senescence-promoting hormones, which would cause the leaves to yellow and degrade faster. Gibberellic acid is used to delay senescence in fruits on trees, but cytokinin is specifically associated with delaying leaf senescence via nutrient mobilisation.

Answer: Cytokinin

124936.subject: Botany
options: Organisms that can live with or without oxygen
Organisms that cannot survive in the presence of oxygen
Organisms that cannot survive in the presence of oxygen
124936.sol: During the process of respiration, oxygen is utilized, and carbon dioxide, water and energy are released as products. The combustion reaction requires oxygen. But some cells live where oxygen may or may not be available. Can you think of such situations (and organisms) where O2 is not available? There are sufficient reasons to believe that the first cells on this planet lived in an atmosphere that lacked oxygen. Even among present-day living organisms, we know of several that are adapted to anaerobic conditions. Some of these organisms are facultative anaerobes, while in others the requirement for anaerobic condition is obligate. In any case, all living organisms retain the enzymatic machinery to partially oxidase glucose without the help of oxygen. This breakdown of glucose to pyruvic acid is called glycolysis.

126899.text:
Assertion : Enzymes lower down the activation energy of the reactant molecule to make its transition into product easier.
Reason : Enzymes are highly substrate specific catalysts.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
126899.sol: Enzymes are highly substrate specific i.e. they catalyze the reaction of a particular substrate only. They facilitate occurrence of a reaction and transition of reactant into product. A chemical reaction $S \rightarrow P$ (where $S$ is the substrate and $P$ the product or products) will take place when a certain number of $S$ molecules at any given instant possess enough energy to attain an activated condition called the 'transition state'. The enzyme combines transiently with the substrate to produce a transient state having a lower energy of activation than that of substrate alone. This results in acceleration of the reaction. Once the products are formed, the enzyme (or catalyst) is free or regenerated to combine with another molecule of the substrate and repeat the process.

128298.text: What is the effect of an impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH?
options: Stimulation of resorption of water and electrolytes
128298.sol: An impairment affecting synthesis or release of ADH results in a diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water leading to water loss and dehydration. This condition is known as Diabetes Insipidus.The pineal gland is located on the dorsal side of forebrain. Pineal secretes a hormone called melatonin. Melatonin plays a very important role in the regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body. For example, it helps in maintaining the normal rhythms of sleep-wake cycle, body temperature. Plasma also contains small amounts of minerals like Na+, Ca++, Mg++, HCO3 –, Cl–, etc. Glucose, amino acids, lipids, etc., are also present in the plasma as they are always in transit in the body. 129453.subject: Zoology
129453.text: How does the toxicity of ammonia, urea and uric acid compare?
options: Ammonia is more toxic than urea and uric acid
Urea is more toxic than ammonia and uric acid
Uric acid is more toxic than ammonia and urea
Ammonia and urea are equally toxic, but uric acid is less toxic
129453.sol: Animals accumulate ammonia, urea, uric acid, carbon dioxide, water and ions like Na+, K+, Cl– , phosphate, sulphate, etc., either by metabolic activities or by other means like excess ingestion. These substances have to be removed totally or partially. In this chapter, you will learn the mechanisms of elimination of these substances with special emphasis on common nitrogenous wastes. Ammonia, urea and uric acid are the major forms of nitrogenous wastes excreted by the animals. Ammonia is the most toxic form and requires large amount of water for its elimination, whereas uric acid, being the least toxic, can be removed with a minimum loss of water.

130613.subject: Zoology
130613.text: Which infections are not completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
options: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes, and HIV infections
130613.sol: Some of these infections like hepatitis–B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing of injection needles, surgical instruments, etc., with infected persons, transfusion of blood, or from an infected mother to the foetus too. Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. Early symptoms of most of these are minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc., in the genital region. Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence, may remain undetected for long. Absence or less significant symptoms in the early stages of infection and the social stigma attached to the STIs, deter the infected persons from going for timely detection and proper treatment. This could lead to complications later, which include pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract. STIs are a major threat to a healthy society.

130897.subject: Zoology
130897.text: What is the secondary follicle characterised by?
130897.sol: The secondary follicle soon transforms into a tertiary follicle which is characterized by a fluid filled cavity called antrum. The theca layer is organized into an inner theca interna and an outer theca externa. It is important to draw your attention that it is at this stage that the primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle grows in size and completes its first meiotic division. It is an unequal division resulting in the formation of a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body. The secondary oocyte retains bulk of the nutrient rich cytoplasm of the primary oocyte. At present we are not very certain about this. The tertiary follicle further changes into the mature follicle or Graafian follicle. The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it. The Graafian follicle now ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovum) from the ovary by the process called ovulation

Assertion is true but the Reason is false

133402.sol: In our body, cell growth and differentiation is highly controlled and regulated. In cancer cells, there is breakdown of these regulatory mechanisms. Normal cells show a property called contact inhibition by virtue of which contact with other cells inhibits their uncontrolled growth. Cancer cells appears to have lost this property. As a result of this, cancerous cells just continue to divide giving rise to masses of cells called tumors. Tumors are of two types: benign and malignant. Benign tumors normally remain confined to their original location and do not spread to other parts of the body and cause little damage. The malignant tumors, on the other hand are a mass of proliferating cells called neoplastic or tumor cells. These cells grow very rapidly, invading and damaging the surrounding normal tissues. As these cells actively divide and grow they also starve the normal cells by competing for vital nutrients. Cells sloughed from such tumors reach distant sites through blood, and wherever they get lodged in the body, they start a new tumor there. This property called metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors.

135413.subject: Zoology
135413.text: A given species of fig tree is pollinated only by its partner wasp species and no other species. The female wasp uses the fruit as an oviposition site and the developing seeds for nourishing its larvae. In return, the wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence. This highly specific relationship demonstrates which of the following ecological interactions and evolutionary phenomena, respectively?
135413.sol:
The interaction between the fig tree and the wasp is mutualism (+, +) because both species derive benefit from each other. The fig tree is pollinated by the wasp, while the wasp gets a safe site for laying eggs (oviposition) and developing seeds to nourish its larvae.

The strict one-to-one relationship, where a specific fig species is pollinated only by its partner wasp species, is a classic example of co-evolution. The evolution of the flower and its pollinator species are tightly linked with one another.

Answer: Mutualism and Co-evolution

303519.text: Determine the distance at which two charges, each equal to $1 \text{ C}$, must be placed so that the force between them is equal to your weight $W$.
303519.sol:
According to Coulomb's law, the electrostatic force between two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ separated by a distance $r$ is given by $F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$.

Given that $q_1 = 1 \text{ C}$, $q_2 = 1 \text{ C}$, and $F = W$.

Substituting these values into the formula, we get $W = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{1 \times 1}{r^2}$.

Rearranging the equation to solve for $r^2$, we obtain $r^2 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 W}$.

Taking the square root of both sides gives $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 W}}$.

303806.subject: Physics
303806.text: An astronomical telescope is to be designed with a magnifying power of $50$ in normal adjustment. If the length of the tube is $102 \text{ cm}$, determine the powers of the objective and the eyepiece.
303806.sol:
For an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the magnifying power is $m = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$ and the tube length is $L = f_o + f_e$.

Given $m = 50$, we have $\dfrac{f_o}{f_e} = 50 \Rightarrow f_o = 50 f_e$.

Given $L = 102 \text{ cm}$, substituting $f_o$ gives $50 f_e + f_e = 102 \text{ cm}$.

$51 f_e = 102 \text{ cm} \Rightarrow f_e = 2 \text{ cm} = 0.02 \text{ m}$.

The focal length of the objective is $f_o = 50 \times 2 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ cm} = 1 \text{ m}$.

The power of the objective is $P_o = \dfrac{1}{f_o} = \dfrac{1}{1} = 1 \text{ D}$.

The power of the eyepiece is $P_e = \dfrac{1}{f_e} = \dfrac{1}{0.02} = 50 \text{ D}$.

303888.subject: Physics
303888.text: A uniform ladder of length $10.0 \text{ m}$ and mass $16.0 \text{ kg}$ rests against a frictionless vertical wall, forming an angle of $37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the wall. The ground is rough. An electrician weighing $60.0 \text{ kg}$ climbs the ladder and remains at a distance of $8.00 \text{ m}$ from the lower end. Determine the normal force and the force of friction exerted by the ground on the ladder, as well as the minimum coefficient of friction required for the electrician to work safely. (Take $g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$)
303888.sol:
Let $N_g$ be the normal force exerted by the ground, $f$ be the frictional force, and $N_w$ be the normal force exerted by the frictionless wall.

Balancing the vertical forces:

$N_g = m_l g + m_e g$

$N_g = (16.0 + 60.0) \times 9.8 = 76.0 \times 9.8 = 744.8 \text{ N} \approx 745 \text{ N}$

Balancing the horizontal forces:

$f = N_w$

Taking torque about the lower end of the ladder. The ladder makes an angle of $37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the vertical wall, so the perpendicular distances for the weights are proportional to $\sin(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$ and for the normal force from the wall is proportional to $\cos(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$:

$N_w L \cos(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}) = m_l g \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) \sin(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}) + m_e g d \sin(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$

$N_w \times 10.0 \times \cos(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}) = 16.0 \times 9.8 \times 5.0 \times \sin(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}) + 60.0 \times 9.8 \times 8.0 \times \sin(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$

$N_w \times 10.0 = (784 + 4704) \tan(37^{}^{{}^{\circ}})$

$N_w \times 10.0 = 5488 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 4116$

$N_w = 411.6 \text{ N}$

Thus, the force of friction is $f = 411.6 \text{ N} \approx 412 \text{ N}$.

The minimum coefficient of friction $\mu$ required for the electrician to work safely is:

$\mu = \dfrac{f}{N_g} = \dfrac{411.6}{744.8} \approx 0.553$

303913.subject: Physics
303913.text: A uniform rod of length $L$ rests on a smooth horizontal table. A particle moving on the table perpendicularly strikes the rod at one end and stops. Determine the distance travelled by the centre of the rod by the time it turns through a right angle. (Note that if the mass of the rod is four times that of the particle, the collision is elastic.)
303913.sol:
Let the mass of the particle be $m and its initial velocity be $v$. Let the mass of the rod be $M$.

Since the particle stops after the collision, by conservation of linear momentum, the velocity of the centre of mass of the rod $v_c$ is given by:

$mv = Mv_c \Rightarrow v_c = \dfrac{mv}{M}$

By conservation of angular momentum about the centre of the rod:

$mv\dfrac{L}{2} = I\omega$

Substituting the moment of inertia of the rod $I = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}$:

$mv\dfrac{L}{2} = \dfrac{ML^2}{12}\omega \Rightarrow \omega = \dfrac{6mv}{ML}$

The time $t$ taken by the rod to turn through a right angle \left(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is:

$t = \dfrac{\theta}{\omega} = \dfrac{\pi/2}{\dfrac{6mv}{ML}} = \dfrac{\pi ML}{12mv}$

The distance $d$ travelled by the centre of the rod during this time is:

$d = v_c t = \left(\dfrac{mv}{M}\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi ML}{12mv}\right) = \dfrac{\pi L}{12}$

304918.subject: Physics
304918.text: Observed from two frames $S_1$ and $S_2$, the acceleration of a particle has an equal magnitude of $4 ext{ m/s}^2$.
options: The acceleration of $S_2$ with respect to $S_1$ may be either zero or $8 ext{ m/s}^2$.
The frames may be moving relative to each other, but neither should be accelerated with respect to the other.
The acceleration of $S_2$ with respect to $S_1$ may be anything between zero and $8 ext{ m/s}^2$.
The frames must be at rest relative to each other.
304918.sol:
Let the acceleration of the particle with respect to frame $S_1$ be $\vec{a}_{p1}$ and with respect to frame $S_2$ be $\vec{a}_{p2}$.

Given $|\vec{a}_{p1}| = 4 \text{ m/s}^2$ and $|\vec{a}_{p2}| = 4 \text{ m/s}^2$.

The acceleration of frame $S_2$ with respect to frame $S_1$ is given by relative motion:

$\vec{a}_{21} = \vec{a}_{p1} - \vec{a}_{p2}$

The magnitude of $\vec{a}_{21}$ is:

$|\vec{a}_{21}| = \sqrt{|\vec{a}_{p1}|^2 + |\vec{a}_{p2}|^2 - 2|\vec{a}_{p1}||\vec{a}_{p2}|\cos\theta}$

where $\theta$ is the angle between the vectors $\vec{a}_{p1}$ and $\vec{a}_{p2}$.

Substituting the given magnitudes:

$|\vec{a}_{21}| = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2 - 2(4)(4)\cos\theta} = \sqrt{32(1 - \cos\theta)}$

Since the value of $\cos\theta$ lies in the range $[-1, 1]$, the magnitude $|\vec{a}_{21}|$ will vary between a minimum and a maximum value:

$|\vec{a}_{21}|_{\text\min} = \sqrt{32(1 - 1)} = 0$

$|\vec{a}_{21}|_{\text\max} = \sqrt{32(1 - (-1))} = \sqrt{64} = 8 \text{ m/s}^2$

Thus, the acceleration of $S_2$ with respect to $S_1$ can be any value between $0$ and $8 \text{ m/s}^2$. This means it may be exactly zero, exactly $8 \text{ m/s}^2$, or anything in between.

Therefore, both statements "may be either zero or $8 \text{ m/s}^2$" and "may be anything between zero and $8 \text{ m/s}^2$" are correct possibilities.

305063.chapter: Bohr's Model and Physics of the Atom
305063.text: When a photon is emitted by a hydrogen atom, it carries momentum. A hydrogen atom emits light of wavelength $656.3 \text{ nm}$. Find the kinetic energy of recoil of the atom. Take the mass of the hydrogen atom to be $1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$.
305063.sol:
The momentum of the emitted photon is given by $p = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$

By conservation of linear momentum, the recoil momentum of the hydrogen atom is equal in magnitude to the momentum of the photon.

The kinetic energy of recoil of the atom is $K = \dfrac{p^2}{2m} = \dfrac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$K = \dfrac{(6.63 \times 10^{-34})^2}{2 \times 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \times (656.3 \times 10^{-9})^2} \text{ J}$

$K = \dfrac{43.96 \times 10^{-68}}{3.34 \times 10^{-27} \times 4.3 \times 10^{-13}} \text{ J} \approx 3.05 \times 10^{-28} \text{ J}$

Converting the energy into electron-volts (eV):

$K = \dfrac{3.05 \times 10^{-28}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \text{ eV} \approx 1.9 \times 10^{-9} \text{ eV}$

305141.text: A $2.0 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is charged to a potential difference of $12 \text{ V}$ and is subsequently connected to an uncharged $4.0 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor. Determine the heat produced during the charge transfer from one capacitor to the other.
305141.sol:
Given:
$C_1 = 2.0 \mu\text{F}$
$V_1 = 12 \text{ V}$
$C_2 = 4.0 \mu\text{F}$
$V_2 = 0 \text{ V}$

The heat produced during the charge transfer is equal to the loss in electrostatic potential energy of the system:

$\Delta H = \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} (V_1 - V_2)^2$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta H = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{2.0 \times 4.0}{2.0 + 4.0} \times (12 - 0)^2 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta H = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{8.0}{6.0} \times 144 \mu\text{J}$

$\Delta H = \dfrac{4}{6} \times 144 \mu\text{J} = 96 \mu\text{J}$
